narration: In the first stage, 3D Head Geometry Learning begins with a multi-view reference video sequence S-ref, from which the subject's head region X-ref is extracted.
The extracted head is processed by Depth Net to predict dense depth maps, while Pose Net estimates the rotational and translational camera poses for each frame.
Flow computation derives motion fields from the 3D geometry, which are used to warp encoded reference features into an aligned canonical feature representation h-c.
A recurrent ConvLSTM temporally aggregates the warped canonical features before a decoder reconstructs a temporally consistent canonical head x-hat-c.
In the fusion mechanism, the canonical head is transformed by the driving pose parameters into x-hat-dri, paired alongside the driving frame s-dri and reference frame s-ref.
A joint Flow and Attention Map Predictor generates bidirectional motion flow fields and attention weighting heatmaps for both the transformed and reference sources.
Features from both sources are warped by the predicted flow fields and modulated by their respective attention maps to isolate trustworthy facial regions.
Finally, the decoder blends the attention-modulated features to synthesize the photorealistic animated driving frame s-hat-dri matching the desired pose.
